blocks.text: Design a minimal AI image generation frontend where users submit a prompt, monitor an accepted asynchronous job, cancel or retry safely, and inspect a completed image. Show numeric progress only when the service provides a trustworthy value; otherwise use an indeterminate waiting state with elapsed context.

Decision surface:
- Can you define a realistic MVP scope?
- Do you handle long-running async jobs cleanly?
- Do you model UI states and error handling?
- Do you think about storage and delivery of generated assets?

steps.title: 1. Prompt submission
steps.text: User enters a prompt and hits Generate. UI validates input and starts a job.

steps.title: 2. Generation state
steps.text: Show a stable waiting state, use determinate progress only when supported, and prevent accidental duplicate jobs with idempotent creation rather than a visual disable alone.

steps.title: 3. Completion
steps.text: Render the image when the job finishes. Offer download or share.

steps.title: 4. Error and retry
steps.text: If the job fails or times out, show a clear error and a retry button.

steps.title: 5. History
steps.text: Show a short history list of recent generations with thumbnails.

blocks.title: Clarifying questions
items: How long does generation typically take?
Do we need progress events or just a spinner?
Should results be stored permanently or expire?
Do we need content moderation in the flow?
What is the rate limit per user?

blocks.title: Asynchronous generation guarantees
items: UI must not freeze during generation.
Users should understand when to wait vs retry.
Jobs should be resumable on page reload.
Storage should be efficient and CDN-backed.

blocks.title: MVP scope vs future scope
rows: MVP can use a simpler transport

blocks.title: Scope checkpoint
blocks.text: A defensible two-week scope prioritizes a reliable prompt-to-image flow, honest lifecycle states, and recoverable commands. Enhancements belong after those core guarantees are measurable.

The client owns prompt and option state, idempotent job commands, lifecycle monitoring, honest progress, safe image presentation, cancellation, retry, and history navigation. The generation service is an abstract asynchronous job contract; model execution and asset storage stay outside the browser.
